description: Grade a program against a task (wai.quantum.grade/1, quantum-providers.md §8.10): each case run with its intent and graded passed, failed or unchecked, with the verdict that decided it and that verdict's layer and limits; each constraint measured; what went wrong with where to look; and whether the program passes. The grade is a job sealed with the service's key, the task and the program in its request, so anyone can run it again and get the same answer: verify_quantum_result works it out again. Quote each case's grade and layer; a case decided by evidence is not proved. Each case's intent is held to the service's bounds before any case runs, and a grade past them is refused with the local command (`wai-quantum grade`).

program.description: The program graded, OpenQASM 3 or 2, or a generator whose integer inputs the cases give.

task.description: What the program must do, in the exercise form (wai-quantum://docs/verdicts): `intent` (one intent or a list, as run_quantum_circuit takes it), or `cases` (at most 16, each {"name", "inputs": a generator's integer inputs, "intent"}); `job` ({"shots", "seed", "noise"}, nothing else); `constraints` (allow, counts, t_count, two_qubit, no_smells, estimate, qubits, inject); a `title` and `task` in words. No `reference`, `wrong` or `hints`: the grade's receipt seals the task whole.

name: grade_quantum_program

anyOf.description: A grade as a host returns it: the request it was asked, and the result with its receipt.

result.description: A grade's result (engine::grade, the provider protocol's section 8.10): a program held to a task's cases, sealed as a job so that anyone can run it again. Its request is {"grade": {"task": a task in the exercise form (exercise.v1.json) with no solution and no known wrong answers, "program": the OpenQASM text}}. The result gives each case's grade (passed, failed or unchecked) with the verdict that decided it and that verdict's layer, each constraint measured, what went wrong with where to look, whether the program passes, and one verdict of every case's checks, which a verifier works out again. The grade's receipt seals the task, the program and the grade together.

cases.description: Each case in the task's order: its name and inputs as the task gives them, its grade, and the verdict of its run with its intent, with that verdict's level, holds and layer beside it.

grade.description: passed: its intents hold, checked as proof or as evidence; failed: one does not hold, or the reader refused the program at the case's inputs; unchecked: neither was decided (no layer reached it, or the run was refused).

verdict.description: How far the engine checked an answer, as one level of an ordered ladder (wai-quantum://docs/verdicts): refused, parsed, executed, evidence, proof; and the layer that decided it, with that layer's limits. A level says how far the engine checked, not that the answer is good: holds says whether the intents held (true, false, or null when none was decided), and layer names what decided them: exact simulation, a stabilizer check, checked rewrites, the answer held to its problem's own checks, agreement of the run's samples with a simulation, samples held to a distribution, physical consistency, random states, or unchecked. A job's result carries one under verdict when the job gives an intent or asks for one, and the receipt seals it; both MCP servers state one beside every answer about a program.

critique.description: The program's smells, each with its lines.

executed.description: The method that ran and its accuracy class, and the distance a compile put between the program and what ran.

items.description: One intent's check: what it asked, whether it held, how strong the check was, how it was made, the layer it stands on and that layer's limits.

distribution.description: The program's distribution, when its outcomes are few enough to list.

expected.description: An expectation intent: the value the intent states.

fit.description: A sampled intent: the test, its statistic, degrees of freedom and p-value, the level, and whether it rejected.

impossible.description: The outcomes sampled that the stated distribution gives probability 0: the first 64, in order.

impossible_outcomes.description: How many outcomes sampled the stated distribution gives probability 0.

layer.description: The layer the check stands on: unchecked when it was not decided.

limits.description: What that layer does not show.

method.description: A sampled intent: the method the samples were run by.

outcomes.description: The outcomes the distribution holds, or the samples' distinct outcomes.

outside.description: An outcomes or a conserves intent: how much lies outside, as probability of the exact distribution or as a fraction of the samples.

attribution.description: Whose energy it is: the job's worker process, or none (the processor packages' over the job's window, every process on the host in it).

concurrent_jobs.description: Other jobs that ran on the host during the window.

counter.description: The package counter as seen: the longest it went between updates, and the smallest step it took.

declared.description: What the stated uncertainty covers, and what it does not.

energy.description: The CPU energy of the job's process as the kernel counts it, with its uncertainty and what it leaves out, or unmetered with the reason.

engine.description: The engine that made the result: the wai-quantum crate's name and version.

passed.description: Whether the program passes the task: every case passed and every constraint holds.

pointer.description: Where to look first, in words; never the solution.

receipt.description: A result's receipt: an Ed25519 signature, by the key it names, over digest = BLAKE3("wai:quantum-service-receipt\x02" ‖ len ‖ request ‖ len ‖ result), each of request and result in its RFC 8785 canonical text (the result without its receipt member), each length 8 bytes big-endian. Whatever members the request and the result hold are sealed, the result's engine and schema among them. The first receipts (no canon member, $defs/first) sealed their writer's compact text under the domain ending \x01; they still verify. wai/extensions/quantum-providers.md section 8.2 states the seal in full, and section 8.4 what a verifier checks.

canon.description: The canonical form the digest is taken over.

digest.description: The digest signed, 32 bytes in lower-case hex.

key.description: The signing key, 32 bytes in lower-case hex.

signature.description: The signature, 64 bytes in lower-case hex.

time.description: When the receipt was issued and, where it states one, until when it is offered, by the signer's clock, in milliseconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z. Absent on a receipt that seals no time (one from a host with no clock, or sealed before receipts stated one). With it, the digest is taken under the domain ending \x03 and ends with len ‖ the canonical text of this member, so the time cannot be changed or taken off (section 8.2).

not_after_ms.description: The first moment the receipt is no longer offered: after issued_ms.
